name: Screen Shake
description: Camera kick driven by a decaying trauma value rather than by scripted shakes. Anything tagged with the `impact` intent adds trauma; trauma falls off on its own, and the offset is trauma raised to traumaExponent — so overlapping hits accumulate into one continuous shake instead of restarting a canned animation and fighting each other. It names no events at all: it is a pure intent sink, so a new emitter that tags itself `impact` shakes the camera without this descriptor changing. It publishes its offset and roll rather than insisting on applying them: where presentation.camera_follow is in the build, the camera composes them into the one view matrix, and this yields. It emits nothing either, deliberately — a shakeStarted event would be one more thing in the catalogue that nobody listens to.

inputs.name: traumaPerImpact
inputs.description: Trauma added by one impact, on a 0..1 scale. Three hits in quick succession reach full shake; one does not.

inputs.name: traumaDecayPerSecond
inputs.description: How fast trauma bleeds off. At the default a single impact is spent in about a quarter of a second.

inputs.name: traumaExponent
inputs.description: Offset is trauma raised to this power. Above 1 it keeps small impacts subtle while leaving headroom for big ones; at 1 every tap shakes the whole screen, which is the usual reason shake gets turned off in options menus.

inputs.name: maxOffset
inputs.description: Peak positional kick at full trauma, in world units.

inputs.name: maxRoll
inputs.description: Peak rotation at full trauma, in radians. Small values read as weight; large ones read as a bug.

outputs.name: trauma
outputs.description: Current 0..1 trauma, before the exponent is applied.
